title: Whether the saints pray for the Church in general: Drelincourt suspends judgment
source_text: XLV. An vero saltem in genere pro Ecclesia Militante orent quidam inter Reformatos pro certo affirmare nolunt, ac judicium suum ea de re suspendunt, ut saepe jam dictus Carolus Drelincurtius, qui censet incertum esse an Sancti pro Ecclesia orent, & istud inter occulta Dei, nec nobis revelata ponit, quia istud Scriptura nullibi clare & expresse docet. De honore B. Virgini exhibendo tom. 2. pag. 106. num. 179. & seqq.
pass_a_gloss: But whether at least in general they pray for the Militant Church, some among the Reformed are unwilling to affirm for certain, and suspend their judgment on that matter, as the often already mentioned Charles Drelincourt, who judges it to be uncertain whether the Saints pray for the Church, and places this among the hidden things of God, not revealed to us, because Scripture nowhere teaches this clearly and expressly. On the honor to be shown to the Blessed Virgin, volume 2, page 106, number 179 and following.
pass_b_english: Whether the saints at least pray for the Church Militant in general, some among the Reformed will not affirm as certain and suspend judgment on the question.

One is Charles Drelincourt, cited often already, who judges it uncertain whether the saints pray for the Church. He places this among God's hidden things, not revealed to us, because Scripture nowhere teaches it clearly and expressly. (On the Honor to Be Shown to the Blessed Virgin, volume 2, page 106, number 179 and following.)

lemmas.gloss: among the hidden things of God

choices.term: inter occulta Dei, nec nobis revelata
choices.english: among God's hidden things, not revealed to us
choices.why: Echoes Deuteronomy 29:29, the Reformed ground for suspending judgment.
